correctness.rationale: Two repeated points force their affine joining line monochromatic. At q>=3 any two intersecting monochromatic lines would force the entire plane monochromatic: through an outside point choose one of >=4 directions excluding the 2 line directions and the direction through their intersection. Every other repeated pair therefore sits on a monochromatic line of a single parallel class; distinct selected lines cannot share a colour because a transversal would be a forbidden intersecting monochromatic line. Conversely any selection of parallel lines with distinct colours and singleton remaining points obeys the condition. Distinct partitions and coefficient counts follow bijectively, including q=2 exception. Standard-library checker exhausts 14 partitions at order 2 and 21147 partitions at order 3 (29 valid), verifies constructive patterns at orders 4,5,7. No unproved extrapolation from finite checks.

value.rationale: A recently defined invariant is classified at the level of every admissible color partition on every affine plane, even non-Desarguesian. Parallel-class rigidity produces an explicit named-palette polynomial and a family with q(q-2) absent chromatic counts. This is substantive structural information absent from the basic, easily constructed equality Lean=q, and contrasts affine parallelism with pairwise-intersecting projective designs.
